families.text: Inter (variable, self-hosted on web; system-ui on iOS and Android)
families.display: Inter. There is no second face any more. A decorative serif across the headlines of a clinical product reads as an editorial about health rather than a tool for managing one, and of everything in this palette it was the single change that most affected how serious the product looks.

typography.minimumRenderedNote: The floor tests/accessibility.spec.ts enforces on rendered text. It used to be 11 while the same file called 13 the minimum for body text — a two-point gap that unread counts, chart axes and tab-bar labels lived in. The gap is closed rather than described: the caption size is now 13 and the floor is the caption size, so the two agree. That is a type-scale decision with a layout consequence on every dense screen, and the layouts were changed to take it rather than the number being nudged to fit them.
typography.scaleNote: Six steps became seven. Both native passes stopped at the same gap: sectionTitle is 18 and screenTitle is 28, and a card that leads a screen wants something between them — every one of them had reached for 22 and typed it. A step nobody can find is a step everybody invents.

targets.why: A control smaller than a fingertip is not a smaller control, it is a control somebody misses while standing in a doorway holding a child. WCAG 2.2 puts the AA floor at 24x24 (SC 2.5.8) and the AAA figure at 44x44 (SC 2.5.5); this design is held to 44 because it is a health app operated one-handed, and everything that is not is listed below with what it measures instead. tests/accessibility.spec.ts reads this list, so an exemption is a line in the contract rather than a line in a test.
targets.exemptions: A link inside a running paragraph, and an input the design hides behind its own label — the label is the target and is measured in its place.

knownUndersized.note: Twenty-four square, the AA floor, and every slide it selects is also reachable from the pause control and by letting the carousel run. Making it 44 would space three dots across 132px and turn a quiet indicator into the loudest thing on the banner.

An inline text action inside a dense row — a provenance note, a call roster line. At 44 it would double the height of every row it sits in. Every one of them has a full-size equivalent elsewhere on the screen.
Only undersized where it is not a button. Where it is one — the profile control in the top bar — it is 44.

contrast.why: A palette is either measured or it is a matter of opinion, and colour is the one part of a design where an opinion held by somebody with ordinary eyesight is worth nothing to the reader who cannot use the result. Every foreground and background this design actually puts together is listed below with the ratio it has to clear, and scripts/check-boundaries.mjs computes each one from the hexes above on every build. A pair that is not listed is a pair nobody has checked, which is why adding a colour combination to the design means adding a row here first. Vital Teal and Mango appear here only against the 3:1 non-text floor: at 2.49:1 and 1.78:1 on white they are brand marks, not labels, and the two ink variants beside them are what carries the words.
contrast.standard: WCAG 2.2 AA. 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text (18.66px bold or 24px and over) and for the visual boundary of a control or a focus indicator (SC 1.4.11). The focus indicator is two rings, not one: no single colour clears 3:1 against both a white card and a forest panel, and controls exist on both. A light inner ring carries the dark grounds and a dark outer ring carries the light ones, so whichever ground it lands on, one of the two is legible. Tying the ring to --amber, which also labels warnings, made the two pull against each other the moment the warning was darkened enough to be readable.

notMeasured.why: Vital Teal measures 2.49:1 on white, which clears nothing. On a light ground it is a fill — the pulse in the mark, a chart band, the filled half of a bar — where no ratio applies because nothing is being read off it. Anything a reader must actually see is drawn in tealInk, which is measured above. On a dark ground it carries meaning and is measured there.
1.78:1 on white. The pulse line in the logo and the inner focus ring, both of which are measured where they land. Never a label; mangoInk is.
A pressed state behind white text, measured as surface-on-indigoDeep above.
A ground. Measured as the background of the pairs that sit on it.
Measured as a boundary against surface above.

Indigo at eight per cent: the fill behind a chart's area and inside a service zone on the map. Nothing is read off it — the line above it and the label beside it are what carry the value — and it is measured nowhere because it is a tint on a white card rather than a ground anything sits on. It exists as a token because two screens were mixing their own, one as a hex with an alpha suffix and one as a fill-opacity, and neither could be checked.
